tagline: Congo's Atlantic port and oil capital on a headland, its wild coast and northern beaches reached only by road.
summary: Pointe-Noire is the Republic of the Congo's principal seaport and economic centre, set on a headland between the sheltered Pointe-Noire Bay and the open Atlantic, and the coastal terminus of the Congo-Ocean Railway. Its long ocean beach — the Côte Sauvage — runs south of the city, while Pointe-Indienne and the Diosso cliffs lie up the coast to the north. The oil economy concentrates business and expatriate movement, yet the coast north and south of the port is entirely road-served today.

demand_signals.label: Oil-industry mobility
demand_signals.note: Pointe-Noire is Congo's oil capital, concentrating corporate, expatriate and offshore-support movement that values fast, reliable transfer.

demand_signals.label: Côte Sauvage & northern beaches
demand_signals.note: The wild ocean beach and the Pointe-Indienne/Diosso coast north of the city are the region's leisure draw, reached only by road.

demand_signals.label: Bay & coastal access
demand_signals.note: The headland and bay geography make several coastal points slow to reach overland, favouring a direct water link.

demand_signals.label: Port & rail gateway
demand_signals.note: As the Congo-Ocean rail terminus and main port, the city concentrates trade-linked travel.

use_cases.title: Northern-coast beach run
use_cases.body: A coastal link from the port bay north to Pointe-Indienne opens the beaches and lighthouse coast to a fast water service rather than a road drive.

use_cases.title: Oil-support transfer
use_cases.body: Fast, reliable transfers for corporate and offshore-support staff between the port bay and coastal points, booked in-app.

use_cases.title: Côte Sauvage bay hop
use_cases.body: A short bay hop from the port to the Côte Sauvage beachfront links the city to its signature ocean beach by water.

use_cases.title: Headland bypass
use_cases.body: Water hops bypass the road detours the headland-and-bay geography forces on overland trips.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Suited to the sheltered bay hops and the ~11nm coastal run to Pointe-Indienne, where short legs and calm bay water favour a fast, quiet craft that holds a schedule.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Reserved for any longer coastal extensions toward the Kouilou river mouth and beyond, where range matters more than frequency.

signature_routes: Pointe-Noire Bay ↔ Pointe-Indienne — coastal cape link to the northern beaches
Port bay ↔ Côte Sauvage beachfront — bay hop to the signature ocean beach
Oil-support transfer hop — port bay to coastal industry points
Headland bypass commuter hop — direct water link around the cape
transit_planning: Congo's transport investment centres on the port, the Congo-Ocean rail line and the coastal road; passenger water transport along the bay and coast is undeveloped, leaving space for a scheduled, bookable tier.

journeys.today: A road drive up the coast to the beach and lighthouse
journeys.with_navier: A direct ~30 min coastal water run to the northern beaches

journeys.today: A road transfer to the ocean beachfront
journeys.with_navier: A short sheltered bay hop to the signature beach

competitive_landscape: There is no organised passenger-vessel operator on the Pointe-Noire coast; the bay and the beaches north and south are reached only by road, so a clean, scheduled foiling tier would open a new mode rather than displace an incumbent.
seasonality: The Congolese coast has a long dry season (roughly May-September) with cooler Benguela-influenced waters and a wetter, warmer season either side; the sheltered bay supports year-round operation while exposed ocean legs are best day-windowed.
regulatory_note: Maritime transport falls under Congo's merchant-marine and port authority (PAPN); passenger-vessel licensing and coastal navigation rules would frame a scheduled service.

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates durable willingness-to-pay for fast, reliable transfer that a premium water tier can capture.
Shows leisure demand funnelled onto roads that a direct water link can serve faster.
